title: Flatness on a union of finite locally free loci
statement: Let T be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], M an O_T-module, and U a family of open subsets indexed by an arbitrary type. Assume that for each index a the ordinary restriction [def-pc-module-pullback] M|U(a) is finite locally free of some natural rank r(a) [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Then M restricted to the union of U(a) is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. No uniform rank, finite covering, or nonemptiness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Proof, third paragraph: identify E on the open locus through its cohomology sheaf; first step of lem-pc-derived-pullback-single-cohomology

proof.text: Refine each U(a) by finite free trivializing opens using [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. These opens cover W, the union of U(a); ranks may vary between members of the cover.

Tensor products commute with open restriction [def-pc-module-pullback]. On a trivializing open, right tensoring with M is a finite direct sum of the identity functor, so is exact. Kernels and exactness of module sheaf sequences are local on an open cover: equivalently apply the exact stalk functors and use their conservativity. Hence right tensoring with M|W is exact. An additive exact functor of abelian categories preserves finite limits and finite colimits, which is the definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. If the indexing family is empty then W is empty, its module category is zero and the same exactness assertion holds. Rank zero also gives the zero tensor functor.
